device.driver: rtumdfdrv (User-Mode Driver Framework, WinUSB-style bulk pipe)
device.open: CreateFileA(path, GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, NULL)
device.io: plain WriteFile/ReadFile on the device handle + FlushFileBuffers after each WriteFile; no DeviceIoControl in the burn path

transport.model: USB Mass-Storage-like CBW/CSW framing over a vendor bulk pipe (NOT real SCSI; custom opcodes 0xF1..0xFB)
transport.write_alignment: union { DWORD dCBWDataTransferLength; struct { BYTE _pad; BYTE opCode; BYTE type; BYTE _pad2; } } ; iIndicator uses the byte at +1 (+2 holds the sub-command 'type')

constants.DRIVER_MAX_XFER: 0x20000 (128 KiB) per USB request on driver side

csw_status_enum.3: CSW_STAT_WFAIL -> bad block during NAND write, remap

csw_sense.meaning: F_COPY_WRITE_TIME (generic STG flag reused as page/mode flag)

handshake_sequence: Sense/poll step: write 43-byte CBW{sig,tag,dataLen=5,flags=0,iInd=0,op,len=0x1C} + 5 raw channel bytes, then read 50-byte CSW; status 2 = BUSY, keep polling
Read 50-byte CSW; verify [0..3]=='USBS' and [4..7]==0x12345678; status at [13]
retry up to 200 times, 200 ms sleep, 20 s timeout; PASS when status==0

csw_layout.note: bCSWStatus was proven at CSW+13 from the 32-bit load at 0x405f7a (ebp-0x9c+13 = ebp-0x8f)

layout.name: Type
layout.note: sub-command / flags (e.g. 0x06 = DDR enable, 0x01 = write chunk)

layout.name: LogicalBlockAddress
layout.note: flash byte address for writes (0x1500000 for hwsetting), page/block index for erase

layout.name: Spare
layout.note: spare/OOB value; when == 0x79 and remap active, high byte carries remap index

layout.name: CRC32
layout.note: CRC32 of the payload for this chunk

0xF3.name: NAND_WRITE
0xF3.note: NAND page program with BBT remap

0xF4.name: EMMC_WRITE
0xF4.note: primary bulk write opcode used everywhere

0x1C.name: SENSE_REQUEST
0x1C.note: frame reads 0x32 (50) bytes back: 43-byte CBW + 5-byte channel frame at 0x405f31

steps: Open device (CreateFile on the interface path)
ReadFlashInfo: read all _FlashInfo fields from GUI controls (flash type/ddr/nand size/block/page/ecc/start addr/trans range/spare/secure/go-jump)
prepareUsbHWBuf + usb_hw_setting_burner: WRITE 0xF5 to LBA 0x1500000 (DRAM init / hwsetting blob, AES-encrypted)
WRITE 0xFA type=0x06 -> DDR enable, then Sleep(1500 ms)
bootloader.tar members written via 0xF4 at computed block addresses (u-boot / LK / FSBL / TEE / BL31 / hw_setting)
emmc_burner / nand_burner / single_burner: write install.img sections per layout.txt
key_burner: secure key bag / SN / MAC handling
factory_burner: factory.tar (layout.txt + env.txt + sn.txt + bootparam.h + enckey.bin) at factory block address
Optional compare pass, then close device

image_layout.container: install.img (tar-like Realtek image with W_FW_* / FW_* named members)

image_layout.unpack_dir: UnTarTmp (tar xvf of the image; per-project Tempfile used as staging)

encryption.notes: Each blob is an AES-CBC ciphertext from byte 0 (there is no plaintext header); decrypt with a zero IV to recover the DDR register program. The 16-byte "common prefix" seen earlier is just the first ciphertext block.

verified_decryption.method: AES-128-ECB, key=abcdef1213572468a1b2c3d49090babe, applied to the WHOLE file (no header skip)
verified_decryption.note: the earlier 'common 16-byte prefix' observation is actually a common 80-byte (5 AES block) prefix

encryption.CORRECTION: Earlier revisions of this spec claimed 'AES-128-CBC with a zero IV' for the hwsetting blobs. That was WRONG. The correct mode is AES-128-ECB. Under CBC with IV=0 the first plaintext block equals the ECB result, so the first register pair looked valid and the rest was dismissed as noise.

mode_proof.method: count 32-bit words landing in known register windows (0x1800xxxx / 0x9800xxxx); random gives ~0%
mode_proof.conclusion: ECB is correct by two orders of magnitude

usb_hwsetting_decrypted.layout: 148 consecutive little-endian (u32 addr, u32 value) pairs
usb_hwsetting_decrypted.tail: after offset 0x460 the address field stops being a register (checksum/signature trailer)

kylin_blobs_target_other_soc.note: the kylin_* blobs decrypt with the same key but address a 0x98xxxxxx register space, not RTD1295's 0x18xxxxxx
kylin_blobs_target_other_soc.conclusion: irrelevant to this board; ignore them

key_files.for_usb_mp_tool/keytemp/: secure-key bag generation inputs: KRSAKeySet*.pem (public), key_set_final_enc.bin, envgroup.txt, bundled openssl_win7 for key ops

reimplementation_notes: The device is a plain WinUSB/UMDF vendor interface; any OS can talk to it via libusb bulk transfers once driver binding is replaced.
All framing is in userspace: 31-byte CBW -> optional payload -> 50-byte CSW. Do not implement real SCSI.
The `0x2B` first request is a status/sense poll, not a real SCSI READ.
iIndicator must be 1 / 0 / 3 for first / middle / last chunk; 2 is reported back by the device as BUSY.
CRC32 in CBWCB[24..27] covers the chunk payload; device verifies it.
Retry policy: 200 attempts, 200 ms sleep, 20 s overall timeout per CSW.
The AES key is a fixed constant; new firmware encryptions must use the same key or the device rejects them.

sector_unit.note: CBWCB.LogicalBlockAddress is a 512-byte sector index for bootloader members; usb_hwsetting uses raw byte address 0x1500000

layout_type_members.description: Layout_Type is a 24-entry x 0x28-byte global array of st_LoadLayoutData in .data, built by the dynamic initializer ??__ELayout_Type@@YAXXZ. set_device_info_value @0x426BD0 copies Layout_Type[n].length into the matching type_deviceInfo.FW_*_Len field.
layout_type_members.note: Member names end with a trailing space; layout.txt parsing matches the full string including that space. FW_PROFILE is skipped when partition count >= 2.
evidence: set_device_info_value @0x426BD0 writes Layout_Type[0].length -> FW_Kernel_Len .. Layout_Type[0x17].length -> FW_Efuse_Programmer_Len
emmc_burner @0x407050 passes Layout_Type[0].buffer with &param_2->FW_Kernel_Len into WriteDevice(0xF4)
ReadUnTarTempFile @0x41E910 loops psVar30 += 1 with uVar21 += 0x28 while uVar21 < 0x3C0 (24 entries)

why_it_works_without_genkeybag.question: Why does this package work even though GenKeyBag.exe is not included?
why_it_works_without_genkeybag.answer: Because this configuration never takes the secure-key path. Three independent gates each route to a skip branch; the shipped SYSTEM.ini satisfies all three. The secure-key, factory and efuse stages are simply never entered.

hwconfig_binary_format.summary: The plaintext format of usb_hwsetting.bin / HwConfig.bin is a flat stream of little-endian u32 instructions. No .config sample is needed to reproduce it.

wrapper.role: hwconfig_to_Hwbinfile outer wrapper: paths, DeleteFileA, dialog access

converter.role: the real per-line parser and binary writer

helpers.0x00404DD0: write u32 byte-by-byte from LSB to MSB (little-endian)
helpers.0x00404D60: hex parser, accepts 0x prefix, upper or lower case
helpers.0x0040DBC8: read one line into an 0x800 buffer

recovered_from.separators: DAT_00435B10 == b' ,' (space and comma); code also skips \0, \t, \n, '#' and '/'

instruction_grammar.note: every field is a little-endian u32; the low 2 bits of the first word select the op
instruction_grammar.decode_rule: first == 0xFFFFFFFF -> end; first == 3 -> nop (2 words); first & 2 -> mask (3 words); first & 1 -> poll (3 words); else write (2 words)
instruction_grammar.special_case: if a mask address is 0xB801A60C and it is the first mask, the next token is a repeat count

trailer.header_16: efabcdaa 13572468 a1b2c3d4 9092baba (bytes[4:12] == AES key[4:12]; first 3 bytes look like a key-byte permutation)
trailer.middle: small field, almost all zero; usb_hwsetting.bin has 80 00*9 23 a0 (trailing 0x23A0 LE, likely a length/checksum tag)
trailer.signature_32: trailing 32-byte MAC over the preceding data
trailer.mac_algorithm: NOT recovered; it is not MD5/SHA of any obvious range. Preserve the existing trailer verbatim when regenerating.

verification.aes_bijection: AES_ECB_encrypt(AES_ECB_decrypt(orig)) == orig for all three files -> ECB mode confirmed
verification.grammar_cross_check: all three files decode with the same grammar; the kylin blobs exercise all four op types (mask/poll/nop/write)

commands: roundtrip <blob.bin>                    # decode -> text -> re-encode, verify lossless
selftest                                # verify all three shipped blobs

hwconfig_binary_format.consequence: You can generate your own hwsetting without GenKeyBag.exe and without a .config sample: write a .config, encode it, reuse the trailer, AES-128-ECB encrypt, then send it with opcode 0xF5 to address 0x1500000.

config_text_parsing.caveat: boot_recoveryDlg.obj (2016-12-08) and boot_recovery.exe (2017-02-14) are NOT the same link. swap() matches only its first 8 bytes in the exe, and parse_line's jump table / string references do not line up. Conclusions below are based on the obj's symbols and relocation table, cross-checked against the exe's strings and imports; the intended logic is consistent between the two.

parse_line.signature: int CBoot_recoveryDlg::parse_line(char *line, unsigned int *out1, unsigned int *out2)

dispatch.prologue: movsx eax,[eax] ; add eax,-0x6d ; cmp eax,0xa ; ja fail ; mov dl,[eax] ; jmp [edx*4]
dispatch.candidate_range: 'm' .. 'w' (11 entries: m n o p q r s t u v w)

branches.behaviour: strtok -> atoh -> *out2; *out1 = 0; then apply the 0x10000000 rule below

special_rule_at_0x094.meaning: encodes a 4-bit mode/flags field in the top nibble and a 28-bit value in the low bits; out1 receives either 1 or (out2 >> 28)

swap.size: 0x18 (24 bytes), zero relocations so the obj listing is final
swap.used_by: the UART/YMODEM path (big-endian header/CRC fields), NOT by the .config converter

evidence: parse_line has no relocation or symbol involving '='; separators are only space/comma/TAB
FUN_00404810 uses FUN_0040D214 with the literal b' ,' and additionally skips \0 \t \n '#' '/'
a full .text scan of boot_recovery.exe finds 0 instances of `cmp <reg>, 0x3D`
all 21 '=' bytes in the image are instruction immediates (e.g. the 0x3D inside `cmp eax,0xC0000000`) or .rsrc icon pixels -- none is a separator string
equals_sign.conclusion: .config syntax is POSITIONAL, not key=value. 'w 0x1801a010 0x1f' is correct; 'addr=0x1801a010 val=0x1f' is treated as an unknown command. Realtek docs that show 'name = value' describe a different tool/format.

atoh_behaviour.status: bit-exact, verified by Unicorn emulation of the real bytes
atoh_behaviour.provenance: the exe's bytes are byte-identical to boot_recoveryDlg.obj section 107, so the emulated code is exactly the shipped parser
disassembly: test cl,cl ; je end    ; empty string -> 0
mov edx,[esp+8]        ; ** edx = ORIGINAL POINTER, set once outside the loop **
cmp cl,'0' ; jl notdec ; cmp cl,'9' ; jg notdec ; movsx edx,cl ; sub edx,0x30 ; jmp commit
notdec: cmp cl,'a' ; jl notlow ; cmp cl,'f' ; jg notlow ; movsx edx,cl ; sub edx,0x57 ; jmp commit
notlow: cmp cl,'A' ; jl notup ; cmp cl,'F' ; jg notup ; movsx edx,cl ; sub edx,0x37 ; jmp commit
notup:  cmp cl,'X' ; je isx ; cmp cl,'x' ; jne end ; isx: xor eax,eax  ; ** 'x' clears eax but NOT edx **
commit: mov cl,[esi] ; shl eax,4 ; add eax,edx ; inc esi ; test cl,cl ; jne loop
atoh_behaviour.algorithm: eax = eax*16 + digit, with an optional leading 0x/0X; stops at the first char outside [0-9a-fA-FxX]; no error signalling

boundary_table.note: upper X and upper digits fine
LEADING space returns 0 -- no whitespace skipping
SILENT truncation at the first bad char
NOT binary -- 'b' is a valid hex digit

atoh_behaviour.no_error_detection: the caller cannot distinguish 'parsed to 0' from 'parse failed' -- both return 0

bug_leading_x_pointer_leak.summary: if the string STARTS with 'x'/'X' (without a leading '0'), edx still holds the original string pointer, so the result becomes pointer-derived garbage that varies with memory layout.
bug_leading_x_pointer_leak.root_cause: 0x00404D6E `mov edx,[esp+8]` is the ONLY initialisation of edx and it sits outside the loop; the 'x' branch at 0x00404DB2 does `xor eax,eax` but does not touch edx, so the subsequent `add eax,edx` adds the pointer.
bug_leading_x_pointer_leak.why_0x_is_safe: in '0x10' the '0' digit first sets edx = 0, so when 'x' clears eax the following add is +0 and parsing continues cleanly.
bug_leading_x_pointer_leak.self_healing: the pointer contribution is shifted left 4 bits per character, so it is pushed out of 32 bits once 4 or more hex digits follow: 'x111' still varies but 'x1111' onwards is stable. Real addresses are 8 hex digits, which is why the bug never surfaced in the shipped files.

for_hand_written_config: always write full hex with the 0x prefix (e.g. 0x1801a010) -- it is the safest form
no spaces before a number (leading space yields 0)
values are hex, never octal or binary: 010 == 16, 0b101 == 0xB101
a typo in the middle of a number silently truncates instead of failing -- double-check addresses
